passages.text: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Doe of the Dawn.” A Psalm of David.
passages.sermon: David wrote this psalm.\r\nHe gave it to the choirmaster.\r\nHe wanted it sung to the tune called “The Doe of the Dawn.”

passages.text: My God, my God, why have You forsaken me? Why are You so far from saving me, so far from my words of groaning?
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
He set it to the tune called “The Doe of the Dawn.”
David speaks to God.
He says, “My God, my God, why have You left me?”
He asks God, “Why are You so far from saving me?”
He says, “You are far from my words when I groan.”
passages.original: לַ֭מְנַצֵּחַ עַל־ אַיֶּ֥לֶת הַשַּׁ֗חַר מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד׃ אֵלִ֣י אֵ֭לִי לָמָ֣ה עֲזַבְתָּ֑נִי רָח֥וֹק מִֽ֝ישׁוּעָתִ֗י דִּבְרֵ֥י שַׁאֲגָתִֽי׃

passages.text: I cry out by day, O my God, but You do not answer, and by night, but I have no rest.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David speaks to God.
David says, “My God, I cry out to You during the day.”
God does not answer David during the day.
David also cries out to God at night.
David does not find rest at night.
passages.original: אֱ‍ֽלֹהַ֗י אֶקְרָ֣א י֭וֹמָם וְלֹ֣א תַעֲנֶ֑ה וְ֝לַ֗יְלָה וְֽלֹא־ דֽוּמִיָּ֥ה לִֽי׃

passages.text: Yet You are holy, enthroned on the praises of Israel.
passages.sermon:
God is holy.
God sits on the praises of Israel.
God receives honor from Israel’s worship.
God is set apart above all.
God rules from the place of Israel’s praise.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֥ה קָד֑וֹשׁ י֝וֹשֵׁ֗ב תְּהִלּ֥וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: In You our fathers trusted; they trusted and You delivered them.
passages.sermon: Our fathers trusted in You.\r\nThey put their trust in You.\r\nYou delivered them.
passages.original: בְּ֭ךָ בָּטְח֣וּ אֲבֹתֵ֑ינוּ בָּ֝טְח֗וּ וַֽתְּפַלְּטֵֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: They cried out to You and were set free; they trusted in You and were not disappointed.
passages.sermon:
The people cried out to You, God.
You set them free.
They trusted in You.
You did not disappoint them.
passages.original: אֵלֶ֣יךָ זָעֲק֣וּ וְנִמְלָ֑טוּ בְּךָ֖ בָטְח֣וּ וְלֹא־ בֽוֹשׁוּ׃

passages.text: But I am a worm and not a man, scorned by men and despised by the people.
passages.sermon:
The speaker feels very low.
The speaker says, "I am a worm."
The speaker says, "I am not a man."
People scorn me.
The people despise me.
passages.original: וְאָנֹכִ֣י תוֹלַ֣עַת וְלֹא־ אִ֑ישׁ חֶרְפַּ֥ת אָ֝דָ֗ם וּבְז֥וּי עָֽם׃

passages.text: All who see me mock me; they sneer and shake their heads: “He trusts in the LORD, let the LORD deliver him; let the LORD rescue him, since He delights in him.”
passages.sermon:
All who see me mock me.
They sneer at me.
They shake their heads at me.
They say, “He trusts in the LORD.
Let the LORD deliver him.
Let the LORD rescue him.
The LORD delights in him.”
passages.original: כָּל־ רֹ֭אַי יַלְעִ֣גוּ לִ֑י יַפְטִ֥ירוּ בְ֝שָׂפָ֗ה יָנִ֥יעוּ רֹֽאשׁ׃ גֹּ֣ל אֶל־ יְהוָ֣ה יְפַלְּטֵ֑הוּ יַ֝צִּילֵ֗הוּ כִּ֘י חָ֥פֵֽץ בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Yet You brought me forth from the womb; You made me secure at my mother’s breast.
passages.sermon:
God, You brought me out of my mother’s womb.
You caused me to be born.
You made me safe at my mother’s breast.
You gave me security as a newborn child.
You cared for me from the very beginning.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ אַתָּ֣ה גֹחִ֣י מִבָּ֑טֶן מַ֝בְטִיחִ֗י עַל־ שְׁדֵ֥י אִמִּֽי׃

passages.text: From birth I was cast upon You; from my mother’s womb You have been my God.
passages.sermon: I depended on You from the very beginning.\r\nYou cared for me from the time I was born.\r\nYou have been my God since I came from my mother’s womb.
passages.original: עָ֭לֶיךָ הָשְׁלַ֣כְתִּי מֵרָ֑חֶם מִבֶּ֥טֶן אִ֝מִּ֗י אֵ֣לִי אָֽתָּה׃

passages.text: Be not far from me, for trouble is near and there is no one to help.
passages.sermon: God, do not stay far from me.\r\nTrouble is close to me.\r\nNo one helps me.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּרְחַ֣ק מִ֭מֶּנִּי כִּי־ צָרָ֣ה קְרוֹבָ֑ה כִּי־ אֵ֥ין עוֹזֵֽר׃

passages.text: Many bulls surround me; strong bulls of Bashan encircle me.
passages.sermon:
Many bulls surround me.
Strong bulls from Bashan encircle me.
They are powerful.
They are close to me on every side.
passages.original: סְ֭בָבוּנִי פָּרִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים אַבִּירֵ֖י בָשָׁ֣ן כִּתְּרֽוּנִי׃

passages.text: They open their jaws against me like lions that roar and maul.
passages.sermon:
My enemies open their mouths against me.
They act like lions.
Lions roar.
Lions attack and tear apart their prey.
My enemies threaten me in the same way.
passages.original: פָּצ֣וּ עָלַ֣י פִּיהֶ֑ם אַ֝רְיֵ֗ה טֹרֵ֥ף וְשֹׁאֵֽג׃

passages.text: I am poured out like water, and all my bones are disjointed. My heart is like wax; it melts away within me.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is suffering greatly.
He feels weak and helpless.
He says, "I am poured out like water."
He feels completely emptied.
He says, "All my bones are disjointed."
His body feels broken and separated.
He says, "My heart is like wax."
His heart is soft and melting.
He says, "It melts away within me."
His courage and strength are gone inside him.
passages.original: כַּמַּ֥יִם נִשְׁפַּכְתִּי֮ וְהִתְפָּֽרְד֗וּ כָּֽל־ עַצְמ֫וֹתָ֥י הָיָ֣ה לִ֭בִּי כַּדּוֹנָ֑ג נָ֝מֵ֗ס בְּת֣וֹךְ מֵעָֽי׃

passages.text: My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue sticks to the roof of my mouth. You lay me in the dust of death.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is suffering greatly.
His strength is gone.
His strength is as dry as a broken piece of pottery.
His tongue sticks to the roof of his mouth.
He is extremely weak and dehydrated.
God places him in the dust of death.
He is close to dying.
passages.original: יָ֘בֵ֤שׁ כַּחֶ֨רֶשׂ׀ כֹּחִ֗י וּ֭לְשׁוֹנִי מֻדְבָּ֣ק מַלְקוֹחָ֑י וְֽלַעֲפַר־ מָ֥וֶת תִּשְׁפְּתֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: For dogs surround me; a band of evil men encircles me; they have pierced my hands and feet.
passages.sermon:
Evil men surround me.
They are like a pack of dogs.
They encircle me on every side.
They pierce my hands.
They pierce my feet.
passages.original: כִּ֥י סְבָב֗וּנִי כְּלָ֫בִ֥ים עֲדַ֣ת מְ֭רֵעִים הִקִּיפ֑וּנִי כָּ֝אֲרִ֗י יָדַ֥י וְרַגְלָֽי׃

passages.text: I can count all my bones; they stare and gloat over me.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is suffering greatly.
He can see all his bones.
His body is weak and exposed.
People look at him.
They stare at him.
They gloat over him.
They take pleasure in his suffering.
passages.original: אֲסַפֵּ֥ר כָּל־ עַצְמוֹתָ֑י הֵ֥מָּה יַ֝בִּ֗יטוּ יִרְאוּ־ בִֽי׃

passages.text: They divide my garments among them and cast lots for my clothing.
passages.sermon:
Evil men surround me.
They take my garments.
They divide my clothes among themselves.
They cast lots for my clothing.
passages.original: יְחַלְּק֣וּ בְגָדַ֣י לָהֶ֑ם וְעַל־ לְ֝בוּשִׁ֗י יַפִּ֥ילוּ גוֹרָֽל׃

passages.text: But You, O LORD, be not far off; O my Strength, come quickly to help me.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The speaker asks the LORD to stay close.
The speaker calls the LORD his strength.
The speaker asks the LORD to come quickly.
The speaker asks the LORD to help him.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֣ה יְ֭הוָה אַל־ תִּרְחָ֑ק אֱ֝יָלוּתִ֗י לְעֶזְרָ֥תִי חֽוּשָׁה׃

passages.text: Deliver my soul from the sword, my precious life from the power of wild dogs.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is in danger.
The speaker asks God for help.
The speaker says, "Deliver my soul from the sword."
The speaker says, "Save my precious life from the power of wild dogs."
The speaker calls his life precious.
The speaker believes God can rescue him.
passages.original: הַצִּ֣ילָה מֵחֶ֣רֶב נַפְשִׁ֑י מִיַּד־ כֶּ֝֗לֶב יְחִידָתִֽי׃

passages.text: Save me from the mouth of the lion; at the horns of the wild oxen You have answered me!
passages.sermon: God, you are my helper.\r\nSave me from the mouth of the lion.\r\nYou have answered me at the horns of the wild oxen.
passages.original: ה֭וֹשִׁיעֵנִי מִפִּ֣י אַרְיֵ֑ה וּמִקַּרְנֵ֖י רֵמִ֣ים עֲנִיתָֽנִי׃

passages.text: I will proclaim Your name to my brothers; I will praise You in the assembly.
passages.sermon:
I will speak about Your name to my brothers.
I will tell them who You are.
I will praise You among the people.
I will honor You in the assembly.
passages.original: אֲסַפְּרָ֣ה שִׁמְךָ֣ לְאֶחָ֑י בְּת֖וֹךְ קָהָ֣ל אֲהַלְלֶֽךָּ׃

passages.text: You who fear the LORD, praise Him! All descendants of Jacob, honor Him! All offspring of Israel, revere Him!
passages.sermon: Those who fear the LORD must praise Him.\r\nAll descendants of Jacob must honor Him.\r\nAll offspring of Israel must revere Him.
passages.original: יִרְאֵ֤י יְהוָ֨ה׀ הַֽלְל֗וּהוּ כָּל־ זֶ֣רַע יַעֲקֹ֣ב כַּבְּד֑וּהוּ וְג֥וּרוּ מִ֝מֶּ֗נּוּ כָּל־ זֶ֥רַע יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: For He has not despised or detested the torment of the afflicted. He has not hidden His face from him, but has attended to his cry for help.
passages.sermon:
God does not despise the suffering of the afflicted.
God does not detest the pain of the afflicted.
God does not hide His face from the afflicted.
God listens when the afflicted cry out to Him for help.
passages.original: כִּ֤י לֹֽא־ בָזָ֨ה וְלֹ֪א שִׁקַּ֡ץ עֱנ֬וּת עָנִ֗י וְלֹא־ הִסְתִּ֣יר פָּנָ֣יו מִמֶּ֑נּוּ וּֽבְשַׁוְּע֖וֹ אֵלָ֣יו שָׁמֵֽעַ׃

passages.text: My praise for You resounds in the great assembly; I will fulfill my vows before those who fear You.
passages.sermon:
I praise You, LORD, in the great assembly.
Many people gather together.
I speak my praise among them.
I keep my promises to You.
I fulfill my vows.
I do this in front of those who fear You.
These people honor and respect You, LORD.
passages.original: מֵ֥אִתְּךָ֗ תְֽהִלָּ֫תִ֥י בְּקָהָ֥ל רָ֑ב נְדָרַ֥י אֲ֝שַׁלֵּ֗ם נֶ֣גֶד יְרֵאָֽיו׃

passages.text: The poor will eat and be satisfied; those who seek the LORD will praise Him. May your hearts live forever!
passages.sermon:
The poor will eat.
The poor will be satisfied.
People who seek the LORD will praise Him.
May your hearts live forever.
passages.original: יֹאכְל֬וּ עֲנָוִ֨ים׀ וְיִשְׂבָּ֗עוּ יְהַֽלְל֣וּ יְ֭הוָה דֹּ֣רְשָׁ֑יו יְחִ֖י לְבַבְכֶ֣ם לָעַֽד׃

passages.text: All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the LORD. All the families of the nations will bow down before Him.
passages.sermon: All people everywhere will remember the LORD.\r\nPeople from every part of the earth will turn to Him.\r\nEvery family from every nation will bow down before the LORD.
passages.original: יִזְכְּר֤וּ׀ וְיָשֻׁ֣בוּ אֶל־ יְ֭הוָה כָּל־ אַפְסֵי־ אָ֑רֶץ וְיִֽשְׁתַּחֲו֥וּ לְ֝פָנֶ֗יךָ כָּֽל־ מִשְׁפְּח֥וֹת גּוֹיִֽם׃

passages.text: For dominion belongs to the LORD and He rules over the nations.
passages.sermon:
The LORD has dominion.
He rules over all nations.
God is the ruler of every people.
God’s authority covers the whole earth.
passages.original: כִּ֣י לַ֭יהוָה הַמְּלוּכָ֑ה וּ֝מֹשֵׁ֗ל בַּגּוֹיִֽם׃

passages.text: All the rich of the earth will feast and worship; all who go down to the dust will kneel before Him— even those unable to preserve their lives.
passages.sermon:
This psalm is by David.
The LORD rules over all nations.
All the rich people on earth will eat.
All the rich people will worship the LORD.
Everyone who goes down to the dust will kneel before the LORD.
This includes those who cannot keep themselves alive.
passages.original: אָכְל֬וּ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוּ֨וּ׀ כָּֽל־ דִּשְׁנֵי־ אֶ֗רֶץ לְפָנָ֣יו יִ֭כְרְעוּ כָּל־ יוֹרְדֵ֣י עָפָ֑ר וְ֝נַפְשׁ֗וֹ לֹ֣א חִיָּֽה׃

passages.text: Posterity will serve Him; they will declare the Lord to a new generation.
passages.sermon:
God rules over all nations.
He is the Lord.
Future generations will serve Him.
People will tell about the Lord to those who come after them.
They will declare Him to a new generation.
passages.original: זֶ֥רַע יַֽעַבְדֶ֑נּוּ יְסֻפַּ֖ר לַֽאדֹנָ֣י לַדּֽוֹר׃

passages.text: They will come and proclaim His righteousness to a people yet unborn— all that He has done.
passages.sermon:
People will come.
They will speak about God's righteousness.
They will tell this to people who are not yet born.
They will declare what God has done.
passages.original: יָ֭בֹאוּ וְיַגִּ֣ידוּ צִדְקָת֑וֹ לְעַ֥ם נ֝וֹלָ֗ד כִּ֣י עָשָֽׂה׃
